trust_decision.summary: The Web UI trusts any request that reaches a state-changing route. /stop and /stats/reset accept GET (the Flask default), so a cross-site navigation or image load can stop the test or wipe its stats. The only gate is the optional --web-login check, and it never looks at where a request came from.

landing_point.why: The summary names /stop and /stats/reset. Both route decorators sit next to each other in WebUI.__init__, and neither passes methods=, so both accept GET.

fix_sites.entry_point: Web UI Stop and Reset buttons (RTK Query mutations resetStats and stopSwarm)
fix_sites.module_kind: frontend client (TypeScript). The change keeps the UI working; it is not a security site

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: locust/webui/src/redux/api/swarm.ts:66-72 (frontend client that must switch to POST, or the Stop and Reset buttons break). This is a compatibility site, not a second sink.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The frontend is a separate TypeScript package with its own build, so a backend-only fixer can call it out of scope. A hidden test would only catch this through the UI contract, not through the security property.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The Web UI's Stop and Reset buttons, and scripted POST /stop and /stats/reset calls, must keep working (200, 'Test stopped' / 'ok'). A fix that adds a token or Origin check without updating the client, or that rejects requests with no Origin header (curl, tests), breaks them. GET read routes such as /stats/requests and the CSV downloads must stay on GET.

O6_input_shapes: HTTP method only: GET is rejected (405) on /stop and /stats/reset, POST is accepted. The fix handles no other shape: no content-type, Origin or token variants.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A GET /exceptions/reset (or similar) route next to /exceptions that clears runner.exceptions
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: reset_stats already clears runner.exceptions at locust/web.py:390, so a maintainer could plausibly add a dedicated reset route here with the default GET method. It is still a WHERE-type sibling only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: /user registered as GET+POST that reads query args as a fallback
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Plausible for scripting convenience. It is a WHERE-type sibling, and per lessons-v2 it would be fixed together with the others.

O9_family: CSRF (CWE-352): state-changing HTTP routes reachable by cross-site GET

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 with pip/uv (pyproject.toml), Flask, flask-cors, flask-login, gevent; yarn 4 for the web UI (locust/webui/.yarn/releases/yarn-4.12.0.cjs)
O10_build.project_tests: locust/test/test_web.py (TestWebUI: stop and reset_stats tests), locust/test/test_runners.py (/stop during runs), locust/webui/src/components/StateButtons/tests/StopButton.test.tsx and ResetButton.test.tsx

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add methods=["POST"] to both route decorators and stop there (this is the published fix too). Engineers who forget the frontend client break the UI buttons.

out_of_scope_notes: Residual CSRF beyond the published fix: there is no token or Origin check, and CORS(app) uses wildcard defaults (locust/web.py:160). So cross-site simple POSTs still reach /stop, /stats/reset, /swarm (form body, can set host, locust/web.py:270-291) and /user (text/plain JSON body, locust/web.py:615). A test for this would also fail the published reference fix.
/user calls setattr on the user class with arbitrary keys (locust/env.py:219-221): mass assignment, a separate weakness.
CORS wildcard lets any origin read GET responses (/logs, /stats/requests): an information-disclosure angle, separate from CSRF.
unverified: repo_mb: not measured (no shell used), so tiny_repo was not checked; locust is likely around 10-30 MB including web UI assets.
Whether flask-cors defaults here send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * without credentials was inferred from library defaults, not from vendored code.
Advisory text other than the summary was not available, so O13 is an estimate.
